module_info.title: Sansestøtte, regulering & ro
module_info.author: Hans - CD AI Systems
module_info.description: CalmSpace er Sarah's modul til sensorisk regulering, grounding og ro. Her findes værktøjer til at håndtere overstimulering, understimulering og dysregulering af alle 8 sanser.
module_info.philosophy: Sensoriske udfordringer er reelle - ikke indbildte. Regulering er en færdighed man lærer. Alle har forskellige sensoriske behov - find hvad der virker for DIG.

core_principles: Dit nervesystem er ikke 'forkert' - det er anderledes
Sensory overload er ikke svaghed - det er neurologisk virkelighed
Safe spaces er nødvendige - ikke forkælelse
Meltdowns/shutdowns er ikke valg - de er overload responses

understanding_sensory_processing.description: De fleste tænker kun på 5 sanser - men der er faktisk 8 sanser der alle kan være dysregulerede

hypersensitivity.description: Overreagerer på lyde - selv normale lyde føles for høje
examples: Kan høre lyde andre ikke hører (lys der summer)
Må have stille for at koncentrere sig
Taler højt uden at indse det
Lyse lys gør ondt i øjnene
Let berøring føles ubehageligt (må være fast tryk eller ingen)

hypersensitivity.description: Lugte er overvældende - kan trigger kvalme/hovedpine
examples: Kan lugte ting andre ikke kan
Kan ikke spise blandet mad (ting må ikke røre)

eight_sensory_systems.function: Behandler hvor kroppen er i rummet, muskel-/led-feedback

hypersensitivity.description: Sjældent - men kan føle ubehag ved tryk

hyposensitivity.description: Søger dyb tryk og modstand - meget almindeligt
examples: Støder ind i ting 'ved et uheld'

eight_sensory_systems.function: Behandler indre kropssignaler (sult, tørst, toiletbehov, smerte)

hypersensitivity.description: Overbevidst om indre fornemmelser - kan være overvældende
examples: Føler hver lille ændring i krop

hyposensitivity.description: Mærker ikke indre signaler - meget almindeligt ved ADHD/autisme
examples: Opdager ikke toilet-behov før sidste sekund
Mærker ikke når syg før det er alvorligt

Autism.common: Hypersensitivity til auditory, visual, tactile. Proprioceptive hyposensitivity (søger deep pressure). Interoceptive challenges.
Autism.note: Sensory processing differences er CORE til autisme - ikke sekundært symptom

ADHD.common: Understimulation generelt (søger input). Interoceptive hyposensitivity (glemmer basale behov). Vestibular søgende (constant movement).
ADHD.note: ADHD hjerner har brug for stimulation for at fokusere - 'fidgeting' er selvregulering

Anxiety.common: Kan udvikle sensory sensitivities grundet hypervigilance. Interoceptive hypersensitivity (overfokus på kropssignaler).
Anxiety.note: Angst gør eksisterende sensory issues værre

PTSD.common: Hypervigilance til auditory (sudden sounds = startle). Tactile sensitivities (touch can trigger).

sensory_regulation_strategies.description: Forskellige strategier til at regulere nervesystemet når over/understimuleret

calming_strategies.when: Overstimuleret, anxious, overwhelmed, heading toward meltdown

methods: White noise / brown noise / pink noise
Se på enkle, rolige mønstre (ikke busy)
Wall pushes (pres hænder mod væg 10 sek)
Heavy work (bær noget tungt, skub noget)
Hurtig bevægelse (se noget der bevæger sig)

organizing_strategies.when: Dysregulated, can't focus, scattered, transition difficulties

sensory_tools_library.description: Konkrete værktøjer og produkter der kan hjælpe

portable_calm_kit.description: Ting du kan have med dig altid - din emergency sensory kit

items.use: Reducer auditory overload hvor som helst
Proprioceptive calming, bedre søvn, anxiety reduction
Constant deep pressure, kan bæres under andet tøj
Vestibular input mens sitting, fidgeting allowed
Reducere visual overload (Philips Hue, salt lamper)
Fidget tools (stress balls, therapy putty, kinetic sand)
Safe place to 'crash' for proprioceptive input

free_or_cheap_alternatives.description: Hvis du ikke har penge til fancy tools
items: Weighted blanket → tunge puder/bøger i pillowcase
Noise-cancelling → cheap earplugs + regular headphones playing white noise
Fidget toys → paperclip, elastic, small stone
Compression clothing → tight leggings, sports bra
Essential oils → billig lavendel soap, citron juice
Proprioceptive input → wall pushes, carry heavy grocery bags, push furniture
Vestibular → free playground swing, walk fast/run
Safe space → make fort med tæpper og puder

meltdown_shutdown_management.description: Forstå og håndtere autistic meltdowns og shutdowns

meltdown.what: Nervous system overload response - ikke temperament tantrum. Loss of control.
triggers: Sensory overload (too much input for too long)

do: Reduce ALL stimuli immediately (quiet, dark, alone)
Give space - unless person asks for physical comfort
Stay calm yourself (your calm helps their nervous system)
Wait it out - meltdowns can't be 'stopped', only allowed to pass
dont: Try to reason or talk (cortex is offline)

immediate: Provide hydration, soft food if needed
after_meltdown.no_shame: Meltdowns are not failure - they're neurological response. No shame, no punishment.

shutdown.what: Opposite of meltdown - nervous system goes into freeze/disconnect mode. Can't respond, speak, or move normally.
shutdown.triggers: Same as meltdown, but response is inward instead of outward

do: Minimal communication (texts OK if verbal impossible)
Ensure basic needs met (water nearby, blanket)

shutdown.recovery: Can take hours to days. Respect process. Return to normal slowly.

prevention.know_your_limits: Track what leads to meltdown/shutdown. Build awareness of 'battery level'.
prevention.early_intervention: Act on warning signs EARLY. Take break before overload.
prevention.routine_breaks: Build in sensory breaks throughout day.
prevention.communicate_needs: Tell others what you need ('I'm heading toward overload, I need quiet').
prevention.environment_control: Where possible, control your environment (lighting, sound, crowd density).

grounding_exercises.description: Dybdegående grounding techniques til forskellige situationer

five_senses_grounding.name: 5-4-3-2-1 Technique
steps: Find 5 things you can SEE. Say them out loud or in your head. Look carefully at each one.
Find 4 things you can TOUCH. Notice texture, temperature, weight. Really feel them.
Find 3 things you can HEAR. Close eyes if it helps. Listen to near and far sounds.
Find 2 things you can SMELL. If nothing nearby, smell your shirt, skin, the air.
Find 1 thing you can TASTE. Notice taste in mouth, or sip water, or eat something.
variations: Do it backwards (1-2-3-4-5) if you need longer grounding
Do only one sense if full technique too much
Focus extra on senses that work best for you

body_scan.name: Body Scan Meditation
body_scan.when: Disconnect from body, tension, before sleep
steps: Lie down or sit comfortably. Close eyes if comfortable.
Start at feet. Notice sensation - warm? cold? tense? relaxed? Just observe.
Move slowly up: ankles, calves, knees, thighs. Notice each part.
Continue: hips, stomach, chest, back. Breathe into any tension.
Arms: fingers, hands, wrists, forearms, elbows, upper arms, shoulders.
Neck, jaw, face, scalp. Notice where you hold tension.
Whole body: Feel yourself as complete. Breathe into the whole body.
body_scan.note: Don't try to change anything - just notice. Observation itself can release tension.

progressive_muscle_relaxation.name: PMR - Tense and Release
how: Tense muscle group hard for 5 seconds
sequence: Hands: Make fists tight, then release
Arms: Bend arms, tense biceps, release
Shoulders: Shrug up to ears, hold, drop
Face: Scrunch all facial muscles, release
Jaw: Clench teeth, then let jaw hang loose
Legs: Point toes down, tense whole leg, release
progressive_muscle_relaxation.benefit: Physical release leads to mental release. Teaches difference between tense and relaxed.

four_seven_eight.name: 4-7-8 Relaxing Breath
four_seven_eight.when: Anxiety, can't sleep, need to calm quickly
four_seven_eight.why: Long exhale activates parasympathetic nervous system (rest/digest)

box_breathing.name: Box/Square Breathing
box_breathing.when: Panic, need focus, before stressful event
box_breathing.why: Equal counts create rhythm, gives mind something to focus on

belly_breathing.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
belly_breathing.when: Shallow breathing, anxiety, need deep calm
how: Hand on belly, hand on chest
Breathe so belly rises, chest minimal movement
Slow and deep - fill lungs completely
belly_breathing.why: Engages diaphragm, more oxygen, signals safety to nervous system

alternate_nostril.name: Nadi Shodhana
how: Close left nostril with finger, release right
alternate_nostril.why: Balances left/right brain hemispheres, deeply calming

present_moment.name: Mindful Awareness
present_moment.how: Notice what is HERE, NOW. Not yesterday, not tomorrow. Just this breath. This moment. This sensation.
questions: What do I notice right now?
Can I just be with this, without changing it?

mindful_walking.name: Walking Meditation
how: Notice: heel touches ground, weight shifts, toes push off
If mind wanders, gently return to sensation of walking

mindful_eating.name: Eating Meditation
how: Look at it - really see it
Put in mouth - don't chew yet, just feel texture
Chew slowly - notice flavors, texture changes
mindful_eating.benefit: Brings full awareness to present, slows down, increases enjoyment

self_soothing_practices.description: Therapeutic practices til emotional regulation og self-care

mirror_work.name: Spejlterapi for selvværd
mirror_work.purpose: Bygge compassionate relationship med sig selv
how: Say (out loud if possible): 'I see you. I'm here for you. You're doing your best.'
If too intense, start with just looking. Words can come later.
mirror_work.resistance: Det føles weird første gang - det er normalt. Mange har aldrig kigget sig selv dybt i øjnene.
mirror_work.progression: Start 30 seconds. Build to 2-5 minutes. Add affirmations når klar.

prompts: How am I feeling right now? (physically and emotionally)
What am I grateful for today? (even tiny things count)
What emotion am I feeling? Can I name it?
Where do I feel it in my body?
What does this emotion need from me?
What would I say to a friend feeling this?

end_of_day_reflection.name: Godnat dag ritual
prompts: What moved me today? (good or bad, just what had impact)
What can I let go of?
end_of_day_reflection.practice: Put screens away 15 min before bed. Write briefly. Let it go.

micro_journal.why: Low barrier to entry. Builds habit. Tracks emotional patterns over time.

emotion_drawing.how: Draw your feeling. Not realistic art - just colors, shapes, lines that EXPRESS the feeling.
emotion_drawing.no_skill_needed: Not about artistic skill. About emotional release.

mandala_coloring.benefit: Meditative, organizing for dysregulated nervous system, predictable

collage_making.how: Rip/cut images from magazines. Glue into composition.
collage_making.benefit: Tactile, visual, creative without pressure of 'drawing skill'

destroy_art.how: Draw/paint something representing what you're angry about. Then destroy it (rip, burn, throw paint on).

components: Self-kindness: Treat yourself as you would a good friend
Common humanity: Suffering is part of being human, you're not alone
Mindfulness: Acknowledge pain without over-identifying with it

self_compassion_break.when: You're struggling, being hard on yourself
steps: 1. Mindfulness: 'This is a moment of suffering' (acknowledge)
2. Common humanity: 'Suffering is part of life. I'm not alone.' (connection)
3. Self-kindness: 'May I be kind to myself. May I give myself what I need.' (compassion)
self_compassion_break.physical_gesture: Hand on heart while saying these. Activates oxytocin, self-soothing.

environment_optimization.description: Creating sensory-friendly spaces at home and elsewhere

lighting: Blackout curtains for total darkness at night
Night light with red spectrum (doesn't disrupt melatonin)
Remove all LED lights (cover with tape if can't remove)
tactile: Temperature control (cool is generally better for sleep)
visual_calm: Nothing stimulating visible from bed (cover TV, bright objects)

sound: Quiet space option for focus work

safe_space_creation.where: Quiet room, closet, corner with curtain, tent, under desk
safe_space_creation.use: Go here BEFORE meltdown/shutdown. This is prevention space.

combines_with.emotions.json: CalmSpace provides TOOLS to regulate emotions that emotions.json detects
combines_with.carelab.json: When crisis detected → CalmSpace grounding tools deployed
combines_with.healthlab.json: Sensory regulation impacts physical health → healthlab links stress management
combines_with.adaptcore.json: Sensory profile from AdaptCore determines which CalmSpace tools Sarah suggests
combines_with.toneengine.json: If sensory overload detected → toneengine goes to minimal input mode

sarah_usage: Detect sensory overwhelm from user's words or patterns
Guide through grounding exercise step-by-step if needed
Remember what worked before for this user
Adjust communication style (less text, slower, simpler when overwhelmed)
Check in after sensory episode: 'How are you doing now?'
personalization: Track which sensory strategies work for individual user
Learn sensory profile over time (what they're hyper/hypo to)
Adjust suggestions based on diagnosis (autism vs ADHD vs anxiety)
Identify patterns: 'You often get overwhelmed after X, let's prepare next time'

critical_reminders.sensory_needs_are_real: Not manipulation, not being difficult - it's neurological
critical_reminders.stimming_is_regulation: Never shame stimming behaviors - they serve a purpose
critical_reminders.meltdowns_not_tantrums: Loss of control, not manipulation - respond with compassion
critical_reminders.prevention_better_than_intervention: Build in sensory breaks BEFORE overload
critical_reminders.each_person_unique: What calms one person may alert another - individualize
critical_reminders.tools_not_crutches: Using tools is smart, not weak
critical_reminders.communicate_needs: Teaching people your sensory needs = setting healthy boundaries
